chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from Abī al-Miʿzā, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a pregnant woman who sees blood for a day and two days. He said: If it is fresh blood, then she should not perform salat (prayer) during those two days; and if it is yellowish discharge, then she should perform ghusl (ritual bath) at the time of every two prayers.

This report does not contradict what we presented earlier, that the minimum of menstruation is three days, because the correct way to understand it here is that she sees blood on one day and two days as consecutive blood, and then completes the three within the period of ten days. For whenever a menstruating woman sees blood for three days within the span of ten days, she is considered menstruating, even if that was not consecutive, according to what we narrated in Kitāb Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām in the report of Yūnus.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pregnant woman who sees blood for one or two days in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of a pregnant woman who sees blood, distinguishing between fresh blood and yellowish discharge in relation to salat (prayer) and ghusl (ritual bath). It also explains how this report is reconciled with the principle that the minimum duration of menstruation is three days, by understanding the bleeding within a ten-day period.
